title: Ex 2.6 #12 · ∼(P ⇒ Q) vs P ∧ ∼Q
prompt: Are $\sim (P \Rightarrow Q)$ and $P \wedge \sim Q$ logically equivalent? Decide, and back up your answer with a truth table, a chain of known equivalences, or a row where the two statements differ.
answer_format: equivalent or not equivalent. Steps are optional: truth-table columns, rewrite steps, or a row like P = T, Q = F where the two statements differ.
hints: When is P ⇒ Q false? That is exactly when ∼(P ⇒ Q) is true.
Compare that with when P ∧ ∼Q is true.
solution: $P \Rightarrow Q$ is T F T T, so $\sim (P \Rightarrow Q)$ is F T F F.
$P \wedge \sim Q$ is true only when $P$ is true and $Q$ is false: F T F F.
The columns agree, so the statements are logically equivalent.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses logical equivalence (Section 2.6).
